title: Evolution of my style and workflow from Unreal 5 + ChatGPT to NB2 to full AI IDE typescript coding
author: Glittering-Chef-4914
selftext:
My project has evolved over the last several months. This is where I'm at now, still a huge WIP that really need some bad art changes and the game mockups I did a few minutes before posting this but wanted to share nonetheless.

I'm currently building the foundation for Jurassic Knights Universe (JKU). The goal is a shared universe of interconnected games across different genres that all share the exact same economy, player profiles, and world logic. Right now I am focused purely on building the core engine and systemic foundations so that when it is time to snap new games together, the architecture fully supports it.

The theme of the world is Mud, Steel, and Scales. It is a mix of WW1 trench warfare and medieval knights, but dinosaurs replace all the vehicles and animals. No magic, no cars. Just plate armor, bolt-action rifles, and dinosaur war machines. Because I am using a shared codebase, the interconnected logic means materials I loot in an action RPG game can be used to craft a weapon in a forge game, which I can then equip on a unit in a tactical battler.

My main methods are to use AI for mockups to get ideas I wouldn't have thought of before and then extract the best elements then redesign the UI from there. I make hundreds of images and sort through them, trying to hand pick. Then from there I do custom edits in photoshop or use natural language to make edits to each asset that I think needs adjustments to look like a proper asset. The two dashboard images here are a before and after of this exact process. I took a regular dev UI dashboard and converted it into an actual game UI that I can use inside the game, which lets me actually build out all my entities and the data for them at the same time.

I've never programmed before, I've always been a 3d artist and have a full time job in the game industry for the last 14 years. My first indie game was in Unreal Engine 5 but since I don't have a programmer anymore I transitioned to solo dev. Now claude opus or gemini handles it all for me and it actually allows me to expand the scope. Features that I would request a programmer to do in days takes me an hour now.

I try to work as modularly as possible. Since I rely on AI to write the code, everything lives in a single shared TypeScript monorepo. I keep all the core engine logic in one folder and the actual game clients in another. I am building a strict Entity Component System (ECS) where data is entirely separated from logic, and game rules never touch rendering code.

Because of this setup, I usually try to code two completely different features at the same time, like a UI layout and a core logic system, so they don't touch each other while the AI is working. While I wait for that and do review passes of the code, I try generating art, laying out UI, and stuff like that.

Would love to answer any questions.

replies.author: Glittering-Chef-4914
replies.body:
the other comments in this chain have the journal breakdowns. basically i used my vibe coded UI, fed it into nano banana 2 and gave it a reference of one of my characters and said match the style and completely redo the UI. important piece of the prompts were: "make sure UI elements are not literal UI but aspects of phsyical book related objects converted into UI, like dog tags, book tabs, bookmarks, leather strips, etc." 

if my vibe code UI was designed badly or i was struggling with ideas i would do something way simpler. i just gave it a picture of a finalized closed book in my style and said: "open this codex intellegience dossier and make it a video game UI display sheet for a ww1 dinosaur RPG listing stats and information about a combat soldier dinosaur. make sure UI elements are not literal UI but aspects of phsyical book related objects converted into UI, like dog tags, book tabs, bookmarks, leather strips, etc."

also on my github you can download the journal, it's the codex app. it is still very buggy right now. [https://github.com/Jurassic-Knights/jurassic-knights-universe](https://github.com/Jurassic-Knights/jurassic-knights-universe)

replies.author: Glittering-Chef-4914
replies.body:
i didn't want to learn another engine and i want to be as hands off as possible building and dressing the actual games. using procedural and strong architectural designs/logic i hope to essentially never have to hand place anything except for very custom stuff or only very broad strokes. and to essentially have AI be my hands myself, i can command it do do a lot of things in a few amount of words when it comes to all that stuff, it's my own personal integrator and if i used an engine it would not be able to have such "physical hands" to do things since it can't operate any of the GUI of most engines except I think godot is the most AI friendly one?

also i didn't want bloat and not use 75% of what an engine has and instead just dev out exactly what i need with AI.  also if i wanted anything custom i wanted to be able to make it right away with AI and you can't edit a commercial game engine like that. at least i think. idk i'm not a programmer.

comments.author: oberpat
comments.body: this looks really sick! I've been trying creating a game with nano banana for the sprites as well and I could really use some pointers if I look at this. The dashboard looks insane too! How are you doing animations? Is this desktop only or how are you handling all these with other devices in mind?

replies.author: Glittering-Chef-4914
replies.body:
Animations will be sprite sheets. I haven't finalized it yet but I tested using a naked body in the correct animation frame poses and then using NB2 to put the characters outfit on the body and it worked well. The tricky part is getting the right naked body frames. Autosprite a web app, makes some good ones that's what I tested for the naked body. But that's for basic stuff like walks. Attacks and things like that I'm trying to wait until resources get better autosprite can do it but it's not perfect one shots yet so I'm back logging it. I try to focus on the dev work that's has the best architectures already existing. 

All games will be desktop and mobile. In my dashboard I have a toggle switch between aspect ratios for mobile and desktop and a logic system that arranges the UI based on aspect ratio. I am carefully trying to design UI/UX that works well for both finger taps and desktop. Having the chunky stylized art style makes it easier without making the desktop look like a shitty mobile port. I am hoping that having more camera space of the game for desktop doesn't make too much of a difference between the gameplay experience on both platforms, but it's just that - hope lol 

It worked fine enough for my action rpg test

comments.author: n0chance_
comments.body: Thanks for sharing. What software are you using? Are you using any agentic things like clawdbot or using code assistants in the IDE? How much $$ are you spending on credit//tokens for programming?

replies.author: Glittering-Chef-4914
replies.body:
I use antigravity ultra subscription because i can make unlimited videos and images with it as well. So $250 per month. I just got claude code pro $17/m so I can do work from my phone. I also get youtube premium and a lot of storage which is nice. 

I would really like to use something like clawdbot for a better memory structure and things like that so i'm not only stuck inside an IDE, but you burn your tokens with clawbot - when i set it up as a test run, just doing a few tasks i burnt through $5 and barely got anything done, barely just set it up basically. it just wouldn't make sense financially compared to unlimited coding and images/videos with google AI ultra. I think within the next month or two there will be subscription alternatives to clawdbot that will make a lot more sense or the current IDE subscriptions will be able to work more like clawdbot. 

So no money on credits or tokens. I could probably downgrade to google AI $50 and be just fine. I don't get anywhere near my limits. i'm not progrmaming 24/7 a day, i have a fulltime day job so i just do tasks here and there throughout the day and a bit more focused sessions in the evening. 

But I have disposable income and this stuff is life changing. If I had to pay $500 a month I would. I can't believe the people who complain about free useage or not wanting to spend $20 a month for literally life changing tools. if i had to hire a 3rd world country programmer or assistant to do any of this stuff it would be several hundreds of dollars all the time, take way longer and not as good results.
